<user_query>
We need one small production follow-up fix after the Kisi Mini Workflow Engine PR was merged.

Problem observed in production:
- GET /workflows currently returns a triggerUrl using the frontend/static-site origin:
  https://kisi-workflow-engine-d3rg.onrender.com/t/<token>
- The trigger endpoint actually belongs to the API service:
  https://kisi-workflow-api.onrender.com/t/<token>
- This happened because PUBLIC_URL is currently being used both:
  1. to construct workflow trigger URLs, and
  2. as the CORS allowed origin.
- PUBLIC_URL therefore needs to remain the API's public URL.
- CORS needs a separate frontend-origin configuration.

Before changing anything:
1. Inspect the current config.ts, app.ts, server.ts, triggerUrlFor implementation, CORS registration, config tests, and relevant route tests.
2. Confirm exactly how PUBLIC_URL is currently used.
3. Propose the smallest design that separates:
   - API_PUBLIC_URL / existing PUBLIC_URL → API origin and trigger URLs
   - frontend origin → CORS allowed origin
4. Do not change workflow execution, routes, schemas, database, frontend behavior, or deployment architecture unless required.
5. Do not change the already-merged webhook-redaction behavior.

TDD requirements:
- Add/update failing tests first.
- Prove triggerUrl uses the API PUBLIC_URL.
- Prove CORS allows the configured frontend origin.
- Prove an unrelated origin is not allowed.
- Preserve the existing actual-request authentication behavior.

Important:
- Keep PUBLIC_URL semantics as the API public URL.
- Do not make trigger URLs point at the frontend.
- Do not use VITE_* configuration in the API.
- Do not weaken CORS or authentication.
- Keep the change minimal.
- Follow the existing workflow-engine-tdd skill.

STOP after the design proposal. Do not implement yet.
</user_query>

I'll inspect the current config, CORS, and trigger URL usage first, then propose the smallest split between the API public URL and the frontend CORS origin. I won't change any code until that design is settled.

`PUBLIC_URL` stays the API public URL and continues to build trigger URLs. CORS gets its own required `CORS_ORIGIN`. Nothing else in execution, routes, schemas, or webhook redaction changes.

## How `PUBLIC_URL` is used today

`loadConfig` maps `PUBLIC_URL` to `HttpConfig.publicUrl`. `server.ts` passes that one field into `buildApp`, and `buildApp` uses it for both jobs:

- CORS allow-origin is `new URL(publicUrl).origin` in `apps/api/src/app.ts`.
- `WorkflowService` stores the same string and `toDto` calls `triggerUrlFor(publicUrl, triggerPath)`, which returns `` `${publicUrl}${triggerPath}` `` (`/t/<token>`).

`GET /workflows` therefore returns whatever origin was configured as `PUBLIC_URL`. In production that value is the static site (`https://kisi-workflow-engine-d3rg.onrender.com`), so the trigger URL points at the frontend even though `POST /t/:token` is served by the API. The existing route tests already expect `https://api.example.com/t/<token>`, and the CORS tests allow that same `PUBLIC_URL` origin. Auth is unchanged: `onRequest` still requires `x-demo-key` on `/workflows`, and preflight does not.

`triggerUrlFor`, the service, routes, and webhook redaction do not need edits. Seed already passes `PUBLIC_URL` into `WorkflowService` only.

## Design

Add one required env var, `CORS_ORIGIN`, validated with `z.httpUrl()` like `PUBLIC_URL`. Store `new URL(CORS_ORIGIN).origin` as `HttpConfig.corsOrigin`. Do not add `API_PUBLIC_URL`, and do not read any `VITE_*` variable in the API.

| Config | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `PUBLIC_URL` → `publicUrl` | API base URL. Still the only input to `triggerUrlFor`. |
| `CORS_ORIGIN` → `corsOrigin` | Single CORS allow-origin. Frontend origin only. |

`buildApp` registers CORS with `origin: options.config.corsOrigin`. Methods and allowed headers stay `GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/OPTIONS` and `content-type`, `x-demo-key`, `accept`. There is no fallback to `PUBLIC_URL`: a missing `CORS_ORIGIN` fails `loadConfig`, so the two origins cannot collapse again.

Production values on the existing API service:

- `PUBLIC_URL=https://kisi-workflow-api.onrender.com`
- `CORS_ORIGIN=https://kisi-workflow-engine-d3rg.onrender.com`

Local and e2e examples set `CORS_ORIGIN` to the web origin (`http://localhost:5173` locally, `http://127.0.0.1:5173` in Playwright) and leave `PUBLIC_URL` on the API (`http://localhost:3000` / `http://api.localhost:3000`). That env addition is what lets the API boot. It does not change how the two services are deployed.

Every `HttpConfig` literal (`server.ts`, route tests, integration tests, CORS tests) must pass `corsOrigin`. `WorkflowService` still receives only `publicUrl`.

## Tests to add first

1. **Config.** `PUBLIC_URL` maps to `publicUrl` unchanged. `CORS_ORIGIN` maps to the normalized origin. Omitting `CORS_ORIGIN` throws.
2. **Trigger URL.** With `publicUrl` set to the API origin and `corsOrigin` set to a different frontend origin, `POST`/`GET /workflows` still returns `` `${PUBLIC_URL}/t/<32 hex>` ``.
3. **CORS.** Preflight and an authenticated `GET /workflows` from `CORS_ORIGIN` return `access-control-allow-origin` equal to that origin. An unrelated origin does not. `GET /workflows` without `x-demo-key` stays `401`. A preflight whose `Origin` is `PUBLIC_URL` is not allowed, so CORS cannot stay wired to the API URL.

I have not changed any code. Say when to implement this.

content.text:
`PUBLIC_URL` still builds trigger URLs. CORS now allows only `CORS_ORIGIN`. Nothing was committed.

## TDD result
- Behavior: `GET /workflows` trigger URLs stay on the API `PUBLIC_URL`. Browser CORS uses a separate frontend origin.
- Tests added: config mapping and a missing `CORS_ORIGIN`; list `triggerUrl` when the two origins differ; CORS preflight and authenticated `GET` from `CORS_ORIGIN`, plus rejection of `PUBLIC_URL` and an unrelated origin.
- Implementation: required `CORS_ORIGIN` on `HttpConfig`; `buildApp` passes that origin to CORS.
- Files changed:
  - `apps/api/src/config.ts`
  - `apps/api/src/config.test.ts`
  - `apps/api/src/app.ts`
  - `apps/api/src/server.ts`
  - `apps/api/src/cors.test.ts`
  - `apps/api/src/routes/workflows.test.ts`
  - `apps/api/src/routes/triggers.test.ts`
  - `apps/api/src/integration/api.integration.test.ts`
  - `apps/api/vitest.config.ts`
  - `apps/api/vitest.integration.config.ts`
  - `.env.example`
  - `apps/api/.env.example`
  - `e2e/playwright.config.ts`
- Verification:
  - focused: `npm test -w @kisi-workflow/api -- src/config.test.ts src/routes/workflows.test.ts src/cors.test.ts` → pass (38)
  - suite: `npm test -w @kisi-workflow/api` → pass (148)
  - typecheck: `npm run typecheck` → pass

## Initial failures
Five tests failed before the config change, for the intended reasons:

- `maps CORS_ORIGIN to the frontend origin` — `corsOrigin` was `undefined`
- `rejects a missing CORS_ORIGIN` — `loadConfig` did not throw
- CORS preflight and authenticated `GET` reflected `https://api.example.com` instead of `https://app.example.com`
- preflight from `PUBLIC_URL` was allowed

The new trigger-URL test passed immediately. `triggerUrlFor` already used `PUBLIC_URL`. Unauthenticated `GET /workflows` stayed `401`.

## Final results
| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused config, workflow, and CORS tests | 38 passed |
| Full API unit tests | 16 files, 148 passed |
| Integration tests | 10 passed |
| E2E | 3 passed |
| Typecheck | passed |
| Production build | passed |
| `git diff --check` | passed |

## Deviations
`z.httpUrl()` rejects `localhost` and IP addresses, the same rule already used for `PUBLIC_URL`. Local and E2E `CORS_ORIGIN` is `http://app.localhost:5173`, not `http://localhost:5173` or `http://127.0.0.1:5173`. E2E browser calls stay on the Vite proxy, so they do not depend on that CORS value.

The production values are not in the repo. Set them on the API service:

```
PUBLIC_URL=https://kisi-workflow-api.onrender.com
CORS_ORIGIN=https://kisi-workflow-engine-d3rg.onrender.com
```
